mainTopic: Rules of order and respect for ברכת כהנים, the Torah reading and the הפטרה, and the פסוקים the people say during ברכת כהנים.
overview: This amud finishes the short prayer the כהנים say after ברכת כהנים, ending with the פסוק 'השקיפה'. רב חסדא, partly through רבי זירא, then gives timing rules. The כהנים keep their fingers spread until they turn away. The caller, the כהנים and the ציבור each wait for the one before to finish, and the כהנים turn and leave only around שים שלום. The same waiting order applies to the ברכה, the אמן, each פסוק and the תרגום at the Torah reading. Next, רבי תנחום in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי gives rules about the הפטרה, uncovering the ark, and when the ציבור may leave after the reading. שמואל's view on leaving seems to differ, but the גמרא shows the two rulings fit shuls with and without a second exit. רבא gives the source from 'אחרי ה׳ אלהיכם תלכו'. Finally, the גמרא lists the פסוקים the people say during ברכת כהנים on a regular day, at מוסף of שבת, and at מנחה of a תענית.

steps.title: End of the כהנים's prayer after the blessing
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים finish their prayer by asking הקב"ה to keep His promise. They quote the פסוק 'Look down from Your holy dwelling, from heaven.'
steps.simpleTranslation: '…what You promised us. Look down from Your holy dwelling, from heaven, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the words of a prayer it began earlier. This is the prayer the כהנים say after they bless the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים say: we did what You commanded, so now do what You promised. They back this up with the פסוק from דברים, which asks הקב"ה to look down and bless ישראל.

phrases.english: what You promised us.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the כהנים's request. The promise is 'and I will bless them' (במדבר 6:27).

phrases.english: Look down from Your holy dwelling
from heaven, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַה שֶּׁהִבְטַחְתָּנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the text of the כהנים's prayer, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים end their prayer by asking הקב"ה to fulfill His promise to bless ישראל, using the פסוק השקיפה.

steps.title: כהנים keep their fingers spread until they turn away
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that the כהנים may not bend their fingers back until they have turned their faces away from the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The כהנים may not bend the joints of their fingers until they turn their faces away from the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: A new rule begins here. רב חסדא tells us that the כהנים must hold their hands in the blessing position until they have fully turned away from the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the ברכה, the כהנים spread their hands and fingers. רב חסדא says they may not relax their hands while still facing the ציבור. The hand position stays until the moment they turn around.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the rules about ברכת כהנים and the Torah reading here

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
The kohanim are not permitted
to bend the joints of their fingers
phrases.notes: Their fingers are spread out for the ברכה, so they may not curl them back yet.

phrases.english: until they turn their faces away from the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים רַשָּׁאִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the כהנים's prayer to practical rules about how ברכת כהנים is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים keep their fingers spread until they have turned away from the ציבור.

steps.title: Each person waits for the previous one to finish
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, quoting רב חסדא, sets an order of waiting. The caller waits for the אמן to end. The כהנים wait for the caller. The ציבור waits for the כהנים. The כהנים wait for the אמן before the next blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: The caller may not call out 'כהנים' until the congregation has finished saying 'אמן.' The כהנים may not begin the blessing until the caller has finished his word. The congregation may not answer 'אמן' until the כהנים have finished the blessing. The כהנים may not begin the next blessing until the congregation has finished saying 'אמן.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא reports a chain of rules from רב חסדא. Each person in ברכת כהנים must wait until the one before him has completely finished speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four links in the chain: caller after אמן, כהנים after caller, ציבור after כהנים, and כהנים after the ציבור's אמן. The point is that no one talks over anyone else. That way every word of the ברכה and every אמן is heard clearly.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports רב חסדא's teachings here
another blessing: the next part of ברכת כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: Two different 'אמן's appear here. The first is the ציבור's answer to the שליח ציבור's ברכה before ברכת כהנים. The last is the answer to each part of ברכת כהנים itself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Chisda:
The caller is not permitted
to call out 'Kohanim'
until the 'amen' is finished from the mouth of the congregation,
phrases.notes: This is the אמן answered to the ברכה of thanks right before ברכת כהנים.

phrases.english: and the kohanim are not permitted
to begin the blessing
until the word is finished from the mouth of the caller,
and the congregation is not permitted to answer 'amen'
until the blessing is finished from the mouth of the kohanim,
and the kohanim are not permitted
to begin another blessing
until the 'amen' is finished from the mouth of the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַקּוֹרֵא רַשַּׁאי לִקְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רב חסדא, adding the order of speaking during ברכת כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No one may begin until the person before him has fully finished: caller, כהנים, and ציבור each wait their turn.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the familiar order in shul today: the caller says 'כהנים,' and then the ברכה and the אמן go back and forth without anyone overlapping.

steps.title: When the כהנים may turn away and leave
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, quoting רב חסדא, rules that the כהנים may turn away only once the שליח ציבור begins שים שלום. They may walk off only once he finishes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: The כהנים may not turn their faces away from the congregation until the שליח ציבור begins 'שים שלום.' They may not uproot their feet and walk away until the שליח ציבור finishes 'שים שלום.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא gives another rule from רב חסדא, this one about the end of ברכת כהנים. It says exactly when the כהנים may turn around and when they may leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate stages. Turning their faces away is allowed once שים שלום starts. Actually moving their feet and leaving must wait until שים שלום is finished. This connects back to step 2, which tied relaxing their fingers to the moment they turn away.

keyTerms.meaning: the last ברכה of שמונה עשרה, said right after ברכת כהנים
to uproot their feet, meaning to move from their place

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's timeline for ending ברכת כהנים: fingers stay spread until the כהנים turn; they turn when שים שלום begins; they leave only when שים שלום ends. Throughout, no one speaks until the previous speaker has finished.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said in the name of Rav Chisda:
The kohanim are not permitted
to turn their faces away from the congregation

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיַּתְחִיל שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר בְּ״שִׂים שָׁלוֹם״,
phrases.english: until the prayer leader begins 'Grant peace,'
and they are not permitted to uproot their feet and walk away
until the prayer leader finishes 'Grant peace.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: אֵין הַכֹּהֲנִים רַשָּׁאִין לְהַחְזִיר פְּנֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב חסדא's rules and covers the very end of ברכת כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים turn away once שים שלום begins and leave only after it ends.

steps.title: Waiting order during the Torah reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes רב חסדא: during קריאת התורה, the ברכה, the אמן, the reading, and the תרגום must each finish before the next one starts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The congregation may not say אמן until the reader finishes the ברכה. The reader may not start reading until the congregation finishes saying אמן. The translator may not start translating until the reader finishes the פסוק. The reader may not start the next פסוק until the translator finishes translating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another rule from רב חסדא, this time about the Torah reading. It sets a step-by-step order so that no two people speak over each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like Step 3, which set a waiting order for ברכת כהנים. Here the same idea is applied to the Torah reading. Each part, the ברכה, the אמן, each פסוק, and each תרגום, must be heard fully before the next part begins.

keyTerms.meaning: The person reading from the ספר תורה
The translator who said each פסוק aloud in Aramaic for the people
The Aramaic translation of the פסוק

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Chisda said:
The congregation is not permitted to answer "amen"
until the blessing is finished from the mouth of the reader,
phrases.notes: This is the ברכה the reader says over the Torah reading.

phrases.english: and the reader is not permitted to read from the Torah
until the "amen" is finished from the mouth of the congregation,
and the translator is not permitted to begin the translation
until the verse is finished from the mouth of the reader,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַקּוֹרֵא רַשַּׁאי לְהַתְחִיל בְּפָסוּק אַחֵר
phrases.english: and the reader is not permitted to begin another verse
until the translation is finished from the mouth of the translator.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement in the same series from רבי זירא quoting רב חסדא. It applies the waiting order idea from ברכת כהנים to the Torah reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During קריאת התורה, the ברכה, the אמן, each פסוק, and each תרגום must each be finished before the next begins.

steps.title: The one who reads the הפטרה must first read from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי: the מפטיר must first read some of the Torah before reading the הפטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who concludes with a reading from the נביאים must first read from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new series of rules from רבי תנחום quoting רבי יהושע בן לוי. The first rule is that the person reading the הפטרה must also read from the Torah first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הפטרה is a reading from the נביאים that comes after the Torah reading. This rule says the one who reads it cannot read only from the נביאים. He must first read from the Torah itself.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who concludes by reading the הפטרה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that the מפטיר gets an עלייה to the Torah before reading the הפטרה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The one who concludes with the Prophets,
phrases.notes: He means the one who reads the הפטרה.

phrases.english: must read from the Torah first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new speaker opens a new series of synagogue rules, moving from the Torah reading to the הפטרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מפטיר must read from the Torah before he reads the הפטרה.

steps.title: The הפטרה waits until the ספר תורה is rolled closed
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי again: the מפטיר may not begin the הפטרה until the ספר תורה has been rolled closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who concludes may not read from the נביאים until the ספר תורה has been rolled up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second rule from the same speakers. It sets when the הפטרה may begin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the מפטיר reads from the Torah first. This step adds a timing rule: after the Torah reading, he must wait until the ספר תורה is rolled closed before starting the הפטרה.

keyTerms.meaning: To conclude with the הפטרה reading

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The one who concludes is not permitted to conclude with the Prophets
until the Torah scroll is rolled up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the רבי תנחום series with a timing rule for the הפטרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הפטרה may not begin until the ספר תורה has been rolled closed.

steps.title: The שליח ציבור should not prepare the ark in front of everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי: the שליח ציבור may not uncover the ark while the congregation is there, out of respect for the ציבור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שליח ציבור may not uncover the ark in front of the congregation, because of the honor of the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third rule from the same speakers, about respect for the people in shul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the covering off the ark takes time. Doing it while everyone sits and waits is disrespectful to the ציבור, so it should be done beforehand. The reason given is כבוד הציבור.

keyTerms.meaning: To uncover, to remove the covering
The ark, the cabinet that holds the ספר תורה

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The prayer leader is not permitted
to uncover the ark in front of the congregation,
because of the honor of the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another rule in the רבי תנחום series, this one based on respect for the congregation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שליח ציבור should not uncover the ark in front of the congregation, because of כבוד הציבור.

steps.title: The congregation stays until the ספר תורה is put away
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום quotes רבי יהושע בן לוי: the ציבור may not leave until the ספר תורה is taken and returned to its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The congregation may not leave until the ספר תורה is taken and put back in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth rule from the same speakers. It tells the congregation when they may leave after the Torah reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking out while the ספר תורה is still out would be disrespectful to it. According to רבי יהושע בן לוי, people must wait until the ספר תורה has been taken and put back in its place.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The congregation is not permitted to leave

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיִּנָּטֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וְיָנֻיחַ בִּמְקוֹמוֹ.
phrases.english: until the Torah scroll is taken and placed in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last rule in the רבי תנחום series, about when the people may leave after the reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציבור may not leave until the ספר תורה has been taken and returned to its place.

steps.title: שמואל: stay until the ספר תורה goes out
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a different measure: the congregation must wait until the ספר תורה goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: they must wait until it goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his own view on the rule from Step 9. He sets a different point for when people may leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said to wait until the ספר תורה is taken and put back in its place, while שמואל says to wait until it has gone out. Both agree the people must show respect by waiting, but they seem to give different stopping points. The next step shows they do not really argue.
steps.whatToRemember: Every rule in this section protects order and respect in shul. Don't talk over the ברכה, the אמן, or the תרגום. Read the הפטרה only after the Torah reading is complete. Don't make the ציבור wait. Don't leave before the ספר תורה is treated with respect.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: until it goes out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different opinion on the rule in Step 9 about when the congregation may leave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the congregation must wait until the ספר תורה goes out.

steps.title: The two opinions fit different shuls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי יהושע בן לוי and שמואל do not really argue. One ruling fits a shul with another exit, and the other fits a shul with no other exit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They don't really argue. One case is where there is another doorway, and the other is where there is no other doorway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes peace between the two rulings from Steps 9 and 10, which gave different times for when people may leave shul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי said to wait until the ספר תורה is taken and put back in its place, and שמואל said to wait until it goes out. The גמרא says both are correct, each for a different kind of building. Whether there is a second door changes how long people must wait so they don't walk away in front of the ספר תורה.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree:
This one is where there is another exit.
That one is where there is no other exit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent argument between Step 9 and Step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases (אוקימתא): each ruling applies to a different building layout
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע בן לוי and שמואל argue about how long the congregation must stay
steps.terutzMaskana: Both rulings are correct; the presence or absence of another exit decides which one applies

steps.title: The source for walking after the ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports that בר אהינא explained the rule from the פסוק 'אחרי ה׳ אלהיכם תלכו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: בר אהינא explained it to me from the פסוק 'After ה׳ your God you shall walk.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the source for the rule that people should not leave ahead of the ספר תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to walk 'after' ה׳‎. בר אהינא read this as showing respect by walking behind the ספר תורה, not in front of it. That explains why the congregation has to wait before leaving.
steps.whatToRemember: People do not leave shul in front of the ספר תורה. How long they wait depends on whether there is another exit, and the source is 'אחרי ה׳ אלהיכם תלכו'.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Bar Ahina explained it to me:
"After ה׳ your God you shall walk."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, בַּר אֲהִינָא אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule that was just explained
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the congregation must not leave ahead of the ספר תורה

steps.title: What do the people say during ברכת כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to a new topic and asks what the congregation says while the כהנים are blessing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the כהנים are blessing the people, what do the people say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about ברכת כהנים, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the listeners, not the כהנים. It asks what words the people should say during each blessing.

phrases.english: At the time when the כהנים are blessing the people,
what do they say?
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the people being blessed, not the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַכֹּהֲנִים מְבָרְכִים אֶת הָעָם, מָה הֵן אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the discussion of shul practice and ברכת כהנים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which words the congregation recites while the כהנים bless them

steps.title: Three 'ברכו' פסוקים from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא in the name of רב חסדא says the people say three פסוקים from תהלים, each beginning 'ברכו ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב חסדא: they say 'Bless ה׳, His angels, mighty in strength...', 'Bless ה׳, all His hosts, His servants who do His will', and 'Bless ה׳, all His works, in all places of His rule; bless ה׳, O my soul.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question with three פסוקים the people say during the blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the כהנים bless the people, the people answer by blessing ה׳. There are three פסוקים, one for each of the three blessings of ברכת כהנים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Chisda said:
"Bless ה׳, His angels, mighty in strength, etc."
phrases.notes: תהלים 103:20. 'וגו׳' means the rest of the פסוק is said too.

phrases.english: "Bless ה׳, all His hosts,
His servants who do His will,"
"Bless ה׳, all His works,
in all places of His rule,
bless ה׳, O my soul."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The people recite תהלים 103:20-22, three פסוקים of 'ברכו ה׳'

steps.title: What do they say at מוסף of שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the people say when the כהנים bless again during מוסף on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: During the מוסף prayers of שבת, what do they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up about a second ברכת כהנים on שבת, setting up a different answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since there is another round of ברכת כהנים at מוסף, the גמרא asks whether the people say different פסוקים this time.

phrases.english: During the מוסף prayers of שבת,
what do they say?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמוּסְפֵי דְשַׁבְּתָא, מָה הֵן אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the question of Step 13 to מוסף of שבת
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוקים the people say during ברכת כהנים at מוסף of שבת

steps.title: The פסוקים for מוסף of שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי says that at מוסף the people say פסוקים from 'שיר המעלות הנה ברכו' and 'ברוך ה׳ מציון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: they say 'A song of ascents: Behold, bless ה׳, all servants of ה׳... Lift your hands in holiness and bless ה׳' and 'Blessed is ה׳ from Zion, Who dwells in Jerusalem, Halleluyah.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי gives a different set of three פסוקים for the מוסף ברכת כהנים on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים also praise ה׳, like the weekday ones, but they come from a different place in תהלים. The third one is not the פסוק right after the first two, and the next step asks about that.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
"A song of ascents:

phrases.aramaic: הִנֵּה בָּרְכוּ אֶת ה׳ כׇּל עַבְדֵי ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
phrases.english: Behold, bless ה׳, all servants of ה׳, etc.

phrases.aramaic: שְׂאוּ יְדֵיכֶם קֹדֶשׁ וּבָרְכוּ אֶת ה׳״,
phrases.english: Lift your hands in holiness and bless ה׳,"
"Blessed is ה׳ from Zion,
phrases.notes: תהלים 135:21. This comes from the next chapter, not right after the first two פסוקים.

phrases.english: Who dwells in Jerusalem, Halleluyah."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At מוסף of שבת they say תהלים 134:1-2 and 135:21

steps.title: Why not say the very next פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the people don't also say 'יברכך ה׳ מציון', which comes right after the first two פסוקים in the same chapter.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them also say 'May ה׳ bless you from Zion,' since it is written in that same passage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אסי's list, asking why the third פסוק is taken from somewhere else instead of the פסוק right next to the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יברכך ה׳ מציון' is the third פסוק of the same short chapter. Skipping it for a פסוק from the next chapter looks strange, so the גמרא asks why.

phrases.english: But let them also say
"May ה׳ bless you from Zion,"
since it is written in that same passage!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of the third פסוק in Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's use of תהלים 135:21 as the third פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The natural third פסוק is the one right after the first two in the same chapter, 'יברכך ה׳ מציון'

steps.title: Start by blessing ה׳, end by blessing ה׳
steps.stepSummary: יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי answers that since they began by blessing הקדוש ברוך הוא, they must end by blessing Him too. 'יברכך' is ה׳ blessing us, so it does not fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה son of רבי שמעון בן פזי said: since he began with blessings of הקדוש ברוך הוא, he ends with blessings of הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining why 'יברכך ה׳ מציון' is skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two פסוקים are people blessing and praising ה׳‎. 'יברכך ה׳ מציון' turns around and has ה׳ blessing a person, which changes the direction. So a פסוק that blesses ה׳‎, 'ברוך ה׳ מציון', is chosen to keep the set consistent.
steps.whatToRemember: During ברכת כהנים the people answer with פסוקים that bless ה׳. On weekdays these are תהלים 103:20-22, and at מוסף of שבת they are 134:1-2 and 135:21. 'יברכך ה׳ מציון' is skipped because the set must begin and end with praise of ה׳.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Blessings of הקדוש ברוך הוא' here means blessings given TO ה׳ (praise), not blessings that ה׳ gives us.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
Since he began
with blessings of the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: מְסַיֵּים בְּבִרְכוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: he ends with blessings of the Holy One, Blessed be He.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle of consistency: the set must end the same way it began
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The people should say the next פסוק in the same chapter, 'יברכך ה׳ מציון'
steps.terutzMaskana: The people must end with a פסוק that blesses ה׳, so they say 'ברוך ה׳ מציון' instead

steps.title: What do the people say at מנחה on a fast day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the people say when the כהנים bless them during מנחה of a תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the afternoon prayer of a fast day, what do the people say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new time when the כהנים bless the people: מנחה on a תענית. It is setting up the next answer by asking which פסוקים the people say then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we heard what the people say during the regular blessing and during מוסף on שבת. Now the גמרא asks about a third time when ברכת כהנים is said, the afternoon of a fast day. The question assumes the people say something different at this time too.

phrases.english: At the afternoon prayer of a fast day, what do they say?
phrases.notes: He means while the כהנים are blessing the people at that מנחה, just like the earlier questions.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמִנְחֲתָא דְתַעֲנִיתָא מַאי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the מוסף discussion (steps 15-18), the גמרא extends the same question to a new occasion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוקים the people say during ברכת כהנים at מנחה of a תענית.

steps.title: Three פסוקים of pleading from ירמיהו
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the people say three פסוקים from ירמיהו asking ה׳ to help us for His name's sake, even though we have sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: They say, 'Though our sins testify against us, ה׳, act for the sake of Your name'; 'Hope of Israel, its savior in a time of trouble, why should You be like a stranger in the land...'; and 'Why should You be like a man who is stunned, like a mighty man who cannot save...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב answers the question: on a fast day the people say three פסוקים in a row from ירמיהו פרק יד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Notice the change in tone. On a regular day and at מוסף the people said praise, 'ברכו ה׳'. On a תענית they say פסוקים that admit our sins and beg ה׳ to save us, which matches the mood of a fast day.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of Your name
The hope of Israel, a name for ה׳
And so on; the פסוק continues

steps.whatToRemember: Each time the כהנים bless, the people answer with fitting פסוקים: 'ברכו ה׳' on regular days, פסוקים from 'הנה ברכו' and 'ברוך ה׳ מציון' at מוסף, and pleading פסוקים from ירמיהו at מנחה of a תענית.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
"Though our sins testify against us,
ה׳, act for the sake of Your name,"
"The Hope of Israel, its savior in a time of trouble,
why should You be like a stranger in the land, etc."
"Why should You be like a man who is stunned,
like a mighty man who cannot save, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At מנחה of a תענית the people say ירמיהו 14:7, 14:8, and 14:9 during ברכת כהנים.
